note: Generated by `cargo run -p ironauth-admin --example log-stream-vectors`. Do not edit by hand: it is what the shipped signer produces.

vectors.name: a well formed batch verifies
vectors.why: the happy path, so a consumer that fails everything is not mistaken for a strict one

vectors.name: a batch lifted into another stream is refused
vectors.why: two streams may share a key; the stream id is what stops a batch moving between them

vectors.name: a replayed position is refused
vectors.why: the cursor sequence is monotonic per stream, so a position already seen is a replay and must not verify

vectors.name: a different cursor id is refused
vectors.why: the position is a pair; signing only the sequence would let the id be rewritten

vectors.name: a miscounted batch is refused
vectors.why: the count is redundant for integrity and kept for diagnosis: a consumer can say whether it got a different NUMBER of events or the same number with different content

vectors.name: tampered events are refused
vectors.why: the integrity case: same count, different content

vectors.name: a malformed signature is refused, not thrown on
vectors.why: a verifier that throws on bad input is a denial of service, not a verifier
